To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) apoptosis is a major mechanism of cell death during HIV infection; (2) macrophages are the major phagocytes for apoptotic cells and are thus the most likely target cells for the recycling of viral genetic information; and (3) the HIV genome may survive in the apoptotic debris of infected T cells and thus be transferred to macrophages, leading to the production of infectious virions.
